newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade active at $67- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade active at $67- feedlots.

text.p: Sales of feedlot cattle in the U.S. Plains were active at $67.00 per cwt, steady with light sales on Monday and late last week, feedlot sources said.
About 30,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and another 30,000 in Kansas, sources said.
Sales were brisk early in the week as packers ensured they had enough live cattle lined up to restart operations following the Memorial Day holiday on Monday, sources said.
Major U.S. meat-packing plants will be closed Monday in observance of the holiday, company officials said.

Packer demand also was strong amid expectations for brisk beef demand at retail meat counters over the three-day holiday weekend, which is typically the most active weekend of the year for beef consumption.
Cattle owners reportedly were not reluctant to sell at the $67.00 level because they still made a profit of $25.00 to $30.00 or more per head, several cattle feeders said.

Also, feedyards were attempting to stay current, particularly with increased cattle numbers expected to be market-ready in June, they said. "We need to sell cattle every week to stay ahead," a Kansas feedyard manager said.
